problem: Map-building navigation needs metric/topological maps and SLAM machinery; it is unclear whether a generative latent model can directly serve as a navigation map from a single house tour video, letting a robot plan routes between two images without further data.
motivation: If a VAE latent manifold were continuous (neighbouring latents correspond to neighbouring places) and complete (distinct places get distinct codes), a shortest path (geodesic) between start and goal latents would decode to a followable image sequence, replacing explicit mapping and planning. The thesis tests this hypothesis on a real house tour video.
key_idea: Train a convolutional VAE with a 4-D latent space on frames from a house tour video, then plan navigation as a geodesic between the encoded start and goal latents (gradient descent on summed decoded-image distance), and map decoded images back to nearest training frames to form a route.
insight: The negative result is informative: geodesic routes contain only a few discontinuous scenes (4/50, 3/50, 2/50 distinct categories vs the manual route), although manually chosen continuous routes are encoded uniquely. This shows a good path exists in the latent space but is not the geodesic under the Euclidean image metric. Two causes are proposed: the VAE keeps global structure but blurs detail, and Euclidean pixel distance is a poor continuity measure (image shifts cost a lot; manual-route neighbours have larger distances than geodesic-route neighbours). In case three (kitchen to bathroom, similar appearance), neighbour-vs-random latent distance difference is near zero, showing perceptual aliasing.
method: VAE map: convolutional encoder/decoder VAE (Keras) with a 4-D latent space, trained on frames resized to 60x60x3 with RMSprop, batch size 20, 2000 epochs; a 2-D latent space was found too poor.
Endpoint encoding: pick start and destination images from the training frames and encode them to z_s and z_d (assumes they lie on the toured line).

Geodesic path planning: initialize 50 equally spaced points on the straight line between z_s and z_d, then repeatedly update each middle point by gradient descent to minimize ||g(z_i)-g(z)|| + ||g(z)-g(z_{i+2})||, with g the decoder.
Route production: decode each path point and replace it by the nearest training frame under squared Euclidean distance to get a real-image route.
Evaluation: compare against a manually chosen continuous route via distinct-scene ratio, neighbour vs random distance differences in image and latent space, and neighbour-distance distributions.

setting.training_data: Frames from one YouTube house tour video (segment 0:37-3:57); abstract says 10000 frames, Chapter 4 says 1000 images at equal intervals, resized to 60x60x3
setting.action_space: none (offline planning of a latent path decoded to an image-sequence route; no robot actions executed)
setting.privileged: Start and goal images are taken from the training frames (on the toured trajectory); manual ideal routes are used for evaluation

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark or SR/SPL metrics; only 3 qualitative cases with route-category ratios (4/50, 3/50, 2/50) and distribution plots.
results: Geodesic routes in latent space were reasonable in room sequence but discontinuous and unusable by a route-following robot; the distinct-scene ratios vs manual routes were 4/50, 3/50 and 2/50 for the three cases. Case three (visually similar kitchen and bathroom) was the worst, with the route collapsing to start and goal only.
limitations: Negative result: routes are discontinuous and cannot be followed by a robot; no real robot or baseline comparison, only three hand-picked cases.
Assumes start/goal are training frames; no localization of new images; VAE blurriness and Euclidean metric cause failures, plus aliasing between similar-looking rooms.
Data inconsistency (10000 vs 1000 frames) and single house/video.
